rows.evidence: Q1: Section 4 (System Application and Verification) and Table 2 - the authors deployed their own ZigBee WSN + fuzzy controller on a farmer's drip system in three plots in Mahoba District (UP, India) and report their own observed valve-opening readings in March-September 2023. Q2: Section 4, last paragraph - the authors state that the sprinkler valve opening values indicated limited water use and that the outcome of the system claims to save 10% water compared with a traditional irrigation system; the technology (sensor network + microcontroller + fuzzy actuation of valves) matches the review's definition of smart irrigation.
rows.notes: Support for the claim is very weak. The only water-saving statement is a single unsupported assertion of 10% saving; no water volumes, no control/traditional treatment data, no method for deriving the figure are given (Table 2 only lists meteorological inputs and valve-opening percentages). Moreover, the review's attribution of a central value near 40% to this study is not found in the text - the study says 10%, which lies below the review's 11-42% range. Q4: no intermediate water-balance variable (applied depth, soil water, ET of treatment vs. control) is measured to explain the saving; valve-opening % is reported without a baseline. Q5/Q6: single district, three plots on one farm. Q7: the remark that the system suits small/medium irrigation areas and that rules need adjustment per situation are not stated as requirements for water saving. Q8: the only stated limitation (star topology, node energy consumption) concerns the network, not the water-saving result. Q9: no dispersion or uncertainty reported. Note that the title says sprinkler but the field test used drip; both are automated by the same controller, so not treated as a technology mismatch for a 'smart irrigation' claim.

notes: Short conference proceeding paper; text is complete (pages 1-12). The paper is mainly a system-design description; the field verification reports communication bit-error rate and valve-opening percentages, and water saving is only asserted (10%) without supporting data.
